findings.title: unsubscribe has no guard for anonymous users or topic access
findings.body: `current_user` is nil for a logged-out user (the action is added to the `ensure_logged_in` list, but see the list context). If it isn't in that list, `current_user.id` raises. The action also changes state on a GET, so it is open to CSRF and link prefetchers. A link scanner or image prefetch can unsubscribe or mute the user. Also, `TopicView.new` runs the access check, but `@topic_view.topic` is used before any redirect or guardian check. Consider requiring a confirmation POST.

findings.title: unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil if the user never visited or tracked the topic. `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500. This is likely for emailed topics, for example a watched category or a mention. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which creates the row. Also, a user who is already at `regular` gets muted by a repeat visit to the link, because the else branch runs. Make the action idempotent.

findings.title: Route defined with a dynamic path that conflicts with topic route
findings.body: The `topicUnsubscribe` route path `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` sits after `topic` at `/t/:slug/:id` with a nearPost segment `/:nearPost`. This may be matched as `nearPost = 'unsubscribe'` by the topic route, which is defined first. Define it before the topic resource.

findings.title: Unescaped topic title rendered via triple-stash
findings.body: `stopNotificiationsText` interpolates `fancyTitle` into an I18n string, and the template renders it with `{{{ }}}`. `fancyTitle` is escaped, but I18n interpolation may not re-escape, and the string includes raw HTML. If fancyTitle is not fully sanitized, this is an XSS vector. Verify the escaping, or escape the title before interpolation.
